purpose: Repair an existing navigation regression encountered during the required company-feature browser checks; no later accounting module is being added.

study.scope: Original Bookr interface on an owned fictional database
study.reproduction: Return from a saved purchase to Day Book, hold that request, click the Bookr home link, then release it. The current link silently loses the action and leaves Day Book visible.

controls.busy: Reflect outstanding application API work through an accessible disabled state and visible progress styling

behavior: Mark Home unavailable while application API requests are pending, including overlapping requests
Restore availability after every request completes or fails
Do not navigate, discard a draft, or change company selection merely because activity finishes
When Home is activated after activity, retain the existing busy, dirty-form and confirmation guards
A failed save must retain its draft; declining the later navigation confirmation keeps it intact
Use a reusable activity tracker rather than controller-specific timing delays
keyboard: Preserve existing Home-link keyboard activation when available; do not bypass modal confirmation
defaults: No pending activity; Home follows its existing navigation behavior
validation: No new accounting or metadata validation
accountingEffect: None. No API payload, ledger, voucher, posting, allocation, company context or balance changes.

verification.unitFirst: Failing tests for activity lifetime, overlapping requests and failure cleanup before new tracker implementation
verification.browser: Deterministic held Day Book response plus failed-save/dirty-confirmation checks, with no timing-wait widening
verification.execution: Serial commands and owned fictional fixtures; preview 4780 is read-only; protected 4315 is excluded

result.previewAudit: Read-only 4780 audit passed; 0 writes and unchanged fictional data.
